hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: Our operational improvements during the year, while handling 5% higher volumes, helped drive improvements to income from railway operations, diluted earnings per share, and railway operating ratio (a measure of the amount of operating revenues consumed by operating expenses). For the full year, we achieved an operating ratio of 66.4%, and an adjusted operating ratio of 65.8% (see our non-GAAP reconciliations beginning on page K26), both of which improved on a year-over-year basis. We remain committed to being a safe, productive, resilient, and efficient railroad with industry-competitive margins.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: Income from railway operations, net income and diluted earnings per share increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily as a result of lower railway operating expenses. The reduction in our operating expenses includes lower net expenses related to the Eastern Ohio Incident and $433 million of gains on the sale of railway lines. Railway operating revenues were slightly lower as decreased fuel surcharge revenue, an adverse mix of traffic, and decreased pricing were nearly offset by increased volumes. Our railway operating ratio improved to 66.4 percent.

message.content: Now let me verify the ratio arithmetic.

**Norfolk Southern Corp. (CIK 702165) — railway operating ratio, FY2024 vs FY2023**

**Answer: Operating efficiency improved markedly in 2024.** The railway operating ratio (railway operating expenses ÷ railway operating revenues) fell to **66.4% in FY2024 from 76.5% in FY2023** — a **9.1 percentage-point improvement** (the 10-K expresses this as a 13% decrease in the ratio). A lower operating ratio means a smaller share of revenue was consumed by expenses, i.e., better efficiency.

**Directly disclosed figures (FY ended Dec 31):**

| Railway operating ratio | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2021 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Percent | 66.4 | 76.5 | 62.3 | 60.1 | 69.3 |

Source: 2024 Form 10-K, Item 1/Item 2 table "Ratio of railway operating expenses to railway operating revenues (railway operating ratio)" (chunk `702165/nsc-20241231:9989`); MD&A table "Railway operating ratio (percent) | 66.4 | 76.5 | 62.3 | (13%) | 23%" (chunk `702165/nsc-20241231:84486`).

**Corroboration by calculation (derived, not directly disclosed):**
- FY2024: operating expenses $8,052M ÷ operating revenues $12,123M = **66.42%** (fact IDs 847174 and 859736, accession 0000702165-25-000008, 10-K filed 2025-02-10).
- FY2023: $9,305M ÷ $12,156M = **76.55%** (fact IDs 847165 and 859727, same accession; the 2023 figures are also in the prior 10-K, accession 0000702165-24-000005, fact IDs 847164 and 859726).

**Management's stated drivers (direct disclosure):** The 10-K attributes the improvement to lower railway operating expenses — including lower net expenses related to the Eastern Ohio Incident and $433 million of gains on sales of railway lines — while revenues were slightly lower (decreased fuel surcharge revenue, adverse traffic mix and lower pricing nearly offset by 5% higher volumes). Management also cites an **adjusted operating ratio of 65.8%** (non-GAAP), which likewise improved year over year (chunk `702165/nsc-20241231:83338` and `:84561`).

**Caveats:** The 2024 improvement is flattered by one-off items (the $433M line-sale gains and lower Eastern Ohio Incident costs), so the reported 66.4% is not purely an operating-efficiency signal; the adjusted 65.8% still shows improvement. Also note 2023's 76.5% was itself an unusually weak year (vs. 62.3% in 2022), so the 2024 gain is partly a rebound. The database snapshot's latest annual report is FY2024; no FY2025 annual figures are available.
